title: VPC peering propagation race causing transient DNS resolver affinity loss for Dedicated tenants
creator: Adrian Lopez
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent failures where tenant pods resolved internal service hostnames to an external/incorrect resolver IP after a planned VPC peering failover or topology change. Symptoms are transient DNS resolution pointing at the wrong resolver cluster followed by elevated 5xxs for short windows (~30-120s) before normalizing. Impacted tenants run multi-az peered VPCs with our Dedicated peering agent.

Root cause hypothesis: Control-plane route advertisements for peered prefixes were published before dataplane NAT/routing/iptables programming completed on the affected hosts. This allowed some packets to traverse to a new egress path where the tenant's per-tenant DNS NAT rules were not yet present, producing DNS queries that hit a different resolver cluster. The asymmetry showed up because return-path programming lagged the forward-path route announcement.

Reproduction steps: 
- Replayed topology change in staging by toggling peering on a small set of hosts while running continuous name-resolution load (kube-dns + stub resolvers).
- Observed identical transient resolution to an alternate resolver pool and correlated with missing iptables DNAT rules on the host for the tenant namespace.
- Packet capture shows initial SYN/UDP to correct resolver, response arriving via alternate path with rewritten source, and the connection being accepted by resolver that is not in tenant ACL.

Immediate mitigation (customer-facing):
- Hotfix shipped to avoid full customer impact: 1) Retroactive reprogramming job (on the affected host pool) to ensure per-tenant NAT rules are present, 2) Short-lived automatic rollback of recent peering changes for the most impacted customers when we detect missing rules.
- Customer comms: Notified three customers on support Tier 1 and offered dedicated rollback window and postmortem.

Permanent fix plan:
1) Control-plane gating: Do not advertise peering routes until dataplane programming handshake acknowledges per-host rule application. Implement a dataplane ACK for route activation.
2) Idempotent dataplane programming: Make iptables/NFT rules insertion atomic and order deterministic on peering events to prevent windows without DNAT rules.
3) Add a dataplane-level health check that validates tenant resolver affinity is correct before flipping route advertisements.
4) Backfill: Run a cluster-wide reconciliation job to ensure no host is missing tenant-specific NAT/ACL rules.

Testing and rollout: 
- Unit and integration tests for dataplane ACK and route gating (PR: see links).
- Chaos test in staging: simulate peering flaps while verifying resolver affinity and route convergence time metrics.
- Canary rollout: 2 hosts in prod (non-customer-facing cluster) -> 10 hosts in a single region with low-traffic tenants -> gradual ramp to 50% of fleet -> full fleet. Monitor: resolver-affinity-failure-rate, per-tenant 5xx rate, route-advertisement-lag metric, dataplane-ack timeout metric.

Rollback plan: emergency toggle to disable new gating and fall back to previous static behavior; also a manual reconciliation script to reprogram rules immediately if needed.

Follow-ups and open work: 
- Add an integration test in CI that simulates peering change and asserts no DNS affinity loss (estimate below).
- Postmortem write-up and runbook for SRE on how to detect & remediate without rolling back peering.
- Expand observability: expose per-host dataplane programming latency and a per-tenant last-successful-reprogram timestamp.

Notes: This ticket coordinates with networking, control-plane, and SRE teams. We need a security review for the dataplane ACK handshake to ensure no spoofing of ACKs across tenant boundaries.
